NOTE:WORKHOUSE_FULL_2026-09-07:hodge-haa.statement: The Hodge-Haar electric resolvent engine v0.6c, and the single document this session most needed and did not have. The b_3 retraction earlier today was argued from OTHER documents' descriptions of this notebook's stored failures -- the exact second-hand reasoning AGENTS.md warns about, committed while retracting a mistake of the same shape. Pinned verbatim so it is never again reasoned about at one remove. Read directly, it settles what its lineage does and does not establish, and the answer is sharper than either earlier account: it COLD reproduces t3 = 5/612 and all twelve signed second-order hops, and computes P V R^2 V P = -1975/124848 times the signed incidence adjacency. Because P V P = -P at SU(3) the canonical third-order folded term is that same R^2 kernel. Its header states the discipline itself -- the agreement with the independently recorded O(u^3) coefficient is "reported as a REGRESSION, not used as an input" -- and its closing block names the open gate in its own words: "Run the SECOND resolvent on the actual depth-3 determinant corpus and cold evaluate P V R V R V P. It must reproduce +1975/62424 * S without using the recorded full third-order coefficient." So this lineage derives a sharp target for the direct term and does not itself evaluate it. That is consistent with both standing records: the referee report's account of the stored failures, and the retraction that restored b_3 on the strength of the abstract- domino engine's 251 gates, which is a different lineage. Nothing here promotes b_3; it stays exactly where the domino engine put it.

LIT:BB_1983:G19.detail: The earliest instance in this web of exactly the obstruction G19 is about, from the Euclidean side. The 0^{++} scaling window closes at 5.6 < beta < 5.7 while the string-tension scaling window of its refs [35, 23] extends, in the paper's own words, "to a much higher value" of beta, and no excited state -- the 1^{+-} carrier channel included -- shows any scaling window at all on the 4^3 x 8 lattice. The paper's own conclusion is that the scaling region for excited states "may then be totally out of present computer and SC possibilities". That is not the last word and must not be read as one: MP_1999, CHEN_2006 and AT_2020_SU3 did reach a continuum-extrapolated SU(3) 1^{+-} in the decades after, on anisotropic lattices with far larger variational bases. What this entry supplies is the other end of the baseline, and FLPS_2026 shows the difficulty is not merely historical -- its 2026 SU(6) update is still pre-continuum with no T1+- plateau despite nine T1+- operators in its basis. It is a comparison and a history, not a bound: nothing here constrains the source transport G19 needs, and no number crosses into a Hamiltonian claim.

RESULT:PREDICTABLE_SOURCE_DRIFT.statement: On one filtered probability space, let M_n be adapted L2 observables, r_n=E[M_(n+1)-M_n|F_n], and xi_(n+1)=M_(n+1)-M_n-r_n. The tail satisfies ||M_N-M_n||_2<=sum_(j=n)^(N-1)||r_j||_2+(sum_(j=n)^(N-1)E Var(M_(j+1)|F_j))^(1/2). ROUTE:G19:griffiths-type-monotonicity-of.detail: proposed 2026-09-03 (Alex): a correlation inequality that holds at every beta and makes the electric-flux free energies F_e(beta) monotone in beta, sector by sector -- the sectors are Z_N-valued, so the non-abelian obstruction to Griffiths' inequalities for Wilson loops need not apply -- would carry the gap from strong to weak coupling the way Griffiths carries Ising order across phases. Closed the same day by a sign, before the inequality itself was attempted: the Ising argument needs the monotone quantity to be INCREASING in beta, and the certified series says the flux gap is DECREASING -- at leading order for every N (the gap is C_F L / (2 sqrt u)), and term by term through fifth order for SU(3) (every slope coefficient (n - 1/2) sigma_n is negative, so the truncated gap falls on all of u > 0). A sector-wise monotonicity, if it holds, bounds the weak-coupling gap from ABOVE by its strong-coupling value; it cannot bound it from below, so it cannot establish a gap at large beta. Reweighting by a power of u flips the small-u direction for every k >= 1 and therefore proves nothing. Whether the monotonicity itself holds for SU(N) is left open and is now irrelevant to this gap. record.detail: proposed 2026-09-03 (Alex): a correlation inequality that holds at every beta and makes the electric-flux free energies F_e(beta) monotone in beta, sector by sector -- the sectors are Z_N-valued, so the non-abelian obstruction to Griffiths' inequalities for Wilson loops need not apply -- would carry the gap from strong to weak coupling the way Griffiths carries Ising order across phases. Closed the same day by a sign, before the inequality itself was attempted: the Ising argument needs the monotone quantity to be INCREASING in beta, and the certified series says the flux gap is DECREASING -- at leading order for every N (the gap is C_F L / (2 sqrt u)), and term by term through fifth order for SU(3) (every slope coefficient (n - 1/2) sigma_n is negative, so the truncated gap falls on all of u > 0). A sector-wise monotonicity, if it holds, bounds the weak-coupling gap from ABOVE by its strong-coupling value; it cannot bound it from below, so it cannot establish a gap at large beta. Reweighting by a power of u flips the small-u direction for every k >= 1 and therefore proves nothing. Whether the monotonicity itself holds for SU(N) is left open and is now irrelevant to this gap. What would revive the route: a functional of the sector free energies, defined without knowledge of the large-beta behaviour, that is increasing in beta at small beta AND whose positivity at large beta implies a gap. None is known; the magnetic ('t Hooft twist) free energies go the other way where Griffiths applies, and that direction proves deconfinement persists upward, not confinement. See ADR 0022.

record.detail: The two rigorous constructions in this repository approach the continuum from opposite ends of the coupling axis, and the target is now the interval between them. From the strong-coupling side SC17 and BA20-BA25 give a volume-uniform physical gap for the actual vacuum, and the thermodynamic continuation gives an infinite-volume vacuum with a closed generator and spectrum in {0} union [4epsilon/3, infinity), for k/epsilon at most lambda_c, the root of 6561 l^4 + 1458 l^3 - 81 l^2 - 72 l + 1 in (1/73, 1/72). From the weak-coupling side the YM_BALABAN_MULTISCALE submission runs a Balaban renormalization group at g_k tending to zero. In Kogut-Susskind normalization lambda_c is g^4 above 288, so the two windows are disjoint and the interval between them is what remains. FIRST, the immediate step. Pure Yang-Mills carries no dimension-five gauge- and E(4)-invariant local operator, so once the marginal dimension-four part is absorbed into the running coupling the residual polymer activity is irrelevant with gain L^-2. That one lemma discharges four things at once: the contraction constant for single-block polymers in the submission's (6.10), the a_k^theta that closes its Theorem 7.1, the constant in its corrected coarse-action subtraction, and the restoration of SO(4) in OS1. It is an operator enumeration plus power counting, it is short, and it is not in this repository. It is the highest-leverage step available. SECOND, the target. A nonperturbative Kotecky-Preiss bound at one physical scale a_ref of order (c_0 Lambda_QCD)^-1, where g is of order one. The submission's (8.14) transports a lattice clustering rate of order kappa_star/a into physical units, which diverges as a tends to zero and therefore gives an ultralocal limit rather than a physical mass gap; the gap has to be read at a fixed physical scale that neither the small-g expansion nor lambda_c reaches. The SC17 thermodynamic theorem already has exactly that shape, with explicit constants, in the complementary window. Repairs already applied to the submission are recorded in its repair record and in the balaban_repair suite: the small-field curvature threshold sign, which supplies the k-independent constants that Theorem 5.1 and hence (6.7) need and which also repairs Proposition 3.4's coercivity; the polymer weight recursion; Theorem 6.2's induction hypothesis; and the coarse-action prefactor. Reflection positivity under blocking is already proved for the centered construction the submission uses, in paper/research_notes/G19_BALABAN_BLOCKING_REFLECTION_POSITIVITY_20260830.md. Still open there: propagating the background-relative averaging constraint, whose remaining obstacle is that scalar interpolation of adjoint values in different fibres is not equivariant.
